gpu.explain: The graphics card. It does the heavy maths of training and chat far faster than the main processor.

vram.explain: The memory on the GPU. A model and its training must fit in it, so it decides which models this machine can train.

ram.explain: The computer's main memory. Parts of a model can move here when the GPU is full. That works, but more slowly.

cpu.explain: The computer's main processor. It can run small models, slowly.

parameters.explain: The numbers a model learned during training. More parameters usually mean a more capable model that needs more memory.

context.explain: How much text the model can keep in view at once, counted in tokens. A longer context fits longer documents and chats.

thinking.explain: Some models write out their reasoning before the reply. That reasoning can be read and edited.

qlora.explain: A way to train a large model on a small GPU. Only a small part is trained, on top of a compressed copy of the model.

moe.explain: Mixture of experts. The model holds many specialist parts and uses only a few for each token, so it runs faster than its size suggests.

token.explain: A piece of text the model reads and writes at a time, such as a short word or part of a word.

temperature.explain: How varied the model's word choices are. A low value gives steady, predictable replies. A high value gives more varied ones.

top_p.explain: Limits the next word to the most likely choices. At 0.9 the model picks only among the words that together cover 90% of the likelihood. A lower value gives safer replies.

system_prompt.explain: The instructions every conversation starts with, before anyone types. They set the model's role, tone and rules.

version.explain: One saved state of the model. The first is the base model as downloaded. Each training adds another, stored as a small change on top of the base.

lora.explain: A way to customise a model by training a small add-on on top of it. The add-on is small, so a version needs little disk space and switches quickly.

delta.explain: Only what training changed in the model's weights, stored on its own. The base model is not copied.

adapter.explain: The small file that holds a version's change. It is applied on top of the base model when the version runs.

engine.explain: A server that loads a model and answers messages. Mesbah has its own and can use others.

quantization.explain: Stores the model's numbers with fewer bits, so it takes less memory. 4-bit needs about a quarter of the memory of 16-bit, with a small loss of quality.

api_key.explain: A secret text that lets a tool use Mesbah. It works with the role of the person who made it.

openai_api.explain: The request format many tools and libraries already use. Tools made for it work with Mesbah after changing the address and the key.

gguf.explain: A single-file model format that Ollama and llama.cpp load. A version is exported to it before Ollama can run it.

vllm.explain: A fast model server for GPUs. It can run on another machine, and Mesbah connects to it by its address.

ollama.explain: A program that runs language models on a personal computer. Mesbah connects to it by its address.
